Confounding Variables

I was wondering if there is a way to nest these variables hierarchically? And also, is there a way to deal with subject versus confounding variables?

Thank you!
Stephanie

Dear MSstats Team

We've recently observed that the p-value calculated by the groupComparison function of MSstats sometimes is (strongly!) affected by other groups in the same dataframe - even when these other groups are not used. messages.body_plain:
Hi Christian,

Yes this is a correct (and intended) behavior. MSstats makes the assumption that the variance of protein abundance is approximately same in all the groups. In some sense, using more groups with similar variances is a proxy for using more replicates. Therefore, even if you only compare two groups, MSstats uses all the groups to estimate the variation at the model fitting stage. This results in better numerical stability, more degrees of freedom, and better sensitivity of each pairwise comparison.

There can of course be experiments where the assumption of similar variance between all the conditions is not verified. In these cases it is best to restrict the modeling to the groups being compared only. But in our experience, the default MSstats case is quite common.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat. Thank you for using MSstats.
Olga

messages.body_plain:
Hello MSstats group,

I just wanted to confirm with you that I'm correctly extracting the number of PSMs and unique peptides from the proteinSummarization function in MSstatsPTM, (should work for TMT as well, but would have to tweak variable names).

example
summary = dataSummarizationPTM_TMT(df, method = "msstats")

peptides = summary$PROTEIN$FeatureLevelData %>%
     select(., ProteinName, PSM) %>%
     mutate(PSM_no_charge = gsub("\\_.*", ", PSM) # remove charge state from PSM
     distinct(., PSM_no_charge, .keep_all = TRUE) # remove sample duplicates
     group_by(ProteinName) %>%
     summarize(peptides = n())

PSMs = summary$Protein$FeatureLevelData %>%
     select(., ProteinName, PSM) %>%
     distinct(., PSM, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
     group_by(proteinName) %>%
     summarize(peptides = n())

I appreciate the help.
Best,
Scott
